 India lead the series 2-0.The hosts were dealt a blow ahead of the match as two of their pacers, Matt Henry or Lockie Ferguson, are unavailable for the match.

 Wellington weather forecast for New Zealand vs. India 3rd T20I
 Heavy rain is forecast across Tuesday morning, with the chance of precipitation sitting at 95% or higher from 7am to 9am before the front clears through and leaves the evening dry.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The oddity in the forecast is the wind.
 Wellington is the windiest city in the country, and the Cake Tin is where that reputation gets tested, but Tuesday evening is expected to bring southeasterlies of only 11 km/h, easing to 8 km/h by the close, with gusts not exceeding 27 km/h.
 What the players will notice instead is the cold. The daytime high is forecast at 14°C, and the temperature is expected to be down to 9°C by 11pm, roughly eight degrees cooler than Christchurch was on Saturday night.

 Chances of rain interrupting play in Wellington
 Though rain is forecast in the morning, it should clear up by the evening before the match starts.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Hourly figures through the match sit at 10% or below, dropping back under 5% for the second innings, which makes an interruption unlikely despite the day's overall rain chance of around 28%.
 The wider picture supports that. Clear skies are forecast from around 10pm, and the following two days in Wellington are expected to be sunny, so the front moving through on Tuesday morning is the last of this system rather than the start of it.
 What happens if the New Zealand vs. India 3rd T20I is stopped by rain?
 Should rain arrive despite the forecast, the match could either be delayed or shortened, with the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method used to set a revised target. A minimum of five overs per side is needed for a result, and a complete washout would see the game abandoned, as there is no reserve day.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement An abandonment would suit India, who would retain their 2-0 lead with two to play and could not then lose the series.
 Hnry Stadium pitch report and dew factor for IND vs NZ 3rd T20I
 A morning of heavy rain followed by a cold, still, humid evening is about the most dew-friendly combination available, and with humidity rising through the second innings, the side bowling last should expect a wet ball. The toss winner is likely to field.
 The surface itself tends to favour the quicks over the spinners, and the first-innings average in T20Is here is 153, well below what both sides have been posting in Christchurch. The square boundaries are short at around 60 metres, which is where New Zealand's lack of a slower-ball specialist may be exposed.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The ground has history on New Zealand's side. The highest T20I total here is 219 for 6, made by the hosts against India, and India have never won a T20I at this venue inside the regulation 20 overs.
 What time does the New Zealand vs. India 3rd T20I start?
 The third T20I between New Zealand and India takes place at the Hnry Stadium, also known as Sky Stadium, in Wellington on Tuesday, October 27, 2026.
 Play is expected to begin at 8 PM local time, which is 12:30 PM IST, with the toss half an hour earlier at 7:30 PM local time, or 12 PM IST.
